claims.text: Tailored metadynamics or replica-exchange sampling of solid-liquid interfaces can accurately and efficiently determine melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an FCC high-entropy alloy.
High-entropy alloys such as CoCrFeMnNi exhibit substantial chemical and configurational disorder.
Explicitly sampling the solid-liquid interfacial region permits calculation of the free-energy difference associated with melting.
Local composition fluctuations and configurations at the solid-liquid interface mediate the melting transition in high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced sampling accelerates rare events at the solid-liquid interface and thereby overcomes kinetic barriers.
Enhanced sampling enables accurate integration of the melting free-energy landscape.
The relevant free-energy landscape includes configurational and thermal entropy contributions.
Gibbs free energy is the thermodynamic criterion for determining stable phase selection.
Computed free-energy differences can be used to derive melting temperature.
Computed free-energy differences can be used to derive enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
Computed free-energy differences can be used to derive the volume change on melting.
The proposed approach is expected to achieve fusion-enthalpy uncertainties of approximately ±1–2 kJ/mol.
The proposed approach is expected to achieve melting-temperature uncertainties of approximately ±20 °C.
The proposed approach will consistently estimate liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across diverse high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The proposed approach will be significantly more efficient than conventional methods.
Traditional calorimetry, standard molecular dynamics, and CALPHAD approaches are computationally intensive or limited in their treatment of interfacial phenomena.
The approach is best suited to high-entropy alloys with simple solid-solution structures.
The approach is less applicable to alloys with substantial phase segregation, strong local ordering, or far-from-equilibrium states.
Sampling-parameter sensitivity may introduce significant variability in some high-entropy-alloy systems.
